name: fig_contraction
title: Sourced integrated thermal contraction of 14 cryostat materials
question: How different are the thermal contractions that CryoLean's differential-contraction model can use?
model: None (reference data). CryoLean's differential_thermal_contraction model uses |L (eps_sample - eps_holder)| <= delta with these values.
data: data/physics/materials.json (14 materials, 11 with a 4 K value); evidence ids tc_001, tc_002, tc_005, tc_006, tc_009, tc_010, tc_012, tc_013, tc_018, tc_019, tc_023, tc_024, tc_025, tc_026, tc_028, tc_029, tc_034, tc_035, tc_036, tc_042, tc_044, tc_047, tc_048, tc_054 (NBS Monograph 29 and NIST cryogenic material fits). The 77-80 K marker is the 80 K row, or 77 K where only that is recorded. Copy in paper/data/fig_contraction.json.
caption: Integrated linear thermal contraction from room temperature to 4 K (circles) and to 77-80 K (squares) for the 14 materials in CryoLean's reference table, in units of 10^-3. PTFE (about 21 x 10^-3) is off scale and labelled; fused silica expands slightly on cooling; sapphire and the two G-10 directions have only 77 K values because the cited fits are not valid at 4 K. The dashed line marks copper at 4 K for reference.
